concerns.text: The plan uses a paired t‑test on success‑rate differences (baseline vs. evolved) for each task pair. Success is a binary outcome, so the normality assumption of the paired t‑test is violated; a McNemar’s test or a non‑parametric alternative (e.g., Wilcoxon signed‑rank on proportions) would be statistically appropriate.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 2 – Efficiency Penalty Calculation & Phase 4 – Reward Modeling
concerns.text: The difficulty model is trained only on the high‑penalty subset (tasks with penalty > 2.0) that was selected using the same efficiency‑penalty metric that later serves as a predictor in the trade‑off analysis. This double‑dip creates selection bias, making the subsequent correlation between penalty and success non‑independent and potentially inflating effect sizes.
